\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جلسہ} (jalsā)}{جلسہ (jalsā)}]{\ur{جلسہ} (jalsā) — a public meeting; a rally}

\label{lesson:UR-C358-jalsa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for string-pulling, then the Urdu for transparent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جلسہ}}
\textbf{\ur{جلسہ}} — \emph{jalsā} — \textquotedblleft{}a public meeting; a rally\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کل} \ur{شام} \ur{میدان} \ur{میں} \ur{جلسہ} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kal shām maidān meṅ jalsā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There will be a rally on the ground tomorrow evening.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جلسہ}} (\emph{jalsā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{jalsa}, \textquotedblleft{}a sitting, a session\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalsā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalsā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kal shām maidān meṅ jalsā ho gā.} — There will be a rally on the ground tomorrow evening.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for string-pulling, then the Urdu for transparent, then say \emph{jalsā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جلسہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A public meeting; a rally\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سربراہ} (sarbarāh)}{سربراہ (sarbarāh)}]{\ur{سربراہ} (sarbarāh) — a head of an organisation}

\label{lesson:UR-C358-sarbarah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for transparent, then the Urdu for a rally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سربراہ}}
\textbf{\ur{سربراہ}} — \emph{sarbarāh} — \textquotedblleft{}a head of an organisation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ادارے} \ur{کے} \ur{سربراہ} \ur{نے} \ur{جلسے} \ur{میں} \ur{بات} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{idāre ke sarbarāh ne jalse meṅ bāt kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The head of the organisation spoke at the rally.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سربراہ}} (\emph{sarbarāh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{sarbarāh}, \textquotedblleft{}a manager\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{sar}, \textquotedblleft{}the head\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ضلع} (zilā)}{ضلع (zilā)}]{\ur{ضلع} (zilā) — a district}

\label{lesson:UR-C358-zila}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a rally, then the Urdu for a head of an organisation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ضلع}}
\textbf{\ur{ضلع}} — \emph{zilā} — \textquotedblleft{}a district\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہمارا} \ur{ضلع} \ur{دریا} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hamārā zilā daryā ke pās hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our district lies by the river.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ضلع}} (\emph{zilā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḍilʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}a side, a part\textquotedblright{}: one part of a province.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اکثریت} (aksariyat)}{اکثریت (aksariyat)}]{\ur{اکثریت} (aksariyat) — a majority}

\label{lesson:UR-C358-aksariyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a head of an organisation, then the Urdu for a district.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اکثریت}}
\textbf{\ur{اکثریت}} — \emph{aksariyat} — \textquotedblleft{}a majority\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اکثریت} \ur{نے} \ur{اس} \ur{تجویز} \ur{کی} \ur{حمایت} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aksariyat ne is tajvīz kī himāyat kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The majority backed this proposal.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اکثریت}} (\emph{aksariyat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{aktharīya}, \textquotedblleft{}the greater part\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{akthar}, \textquotedblleft{}more, most\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for giving reasons and opinions.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹھکرانا} (ṭhukrānā)}{ٹھکرانا (ṭhukrānā)}]{\ur{ٹھکرانا} (ṭhukrānā) — to spurn; to turn down flatly}

\label{lesson:UR-C358-thukrana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a district, then the Urdu for a majority.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹھکرانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھکرانا}} — \emph{ṭhukrānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to spurn; to turn down flatly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جلسے} \ur{نے} \ur{اس} \ur{کی} \ur{تجویز} \ur{ٹھکرا} \ur{دی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jalse ne us kī tajvīz ṭhukrā dī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The meeting flatly turned down his proposal.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مشورہ} \ur{ٹھکرایا}, \emph{us ne mashvarā ṭhukrāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹھکرانا}} (\emph{ṭhukrānā}) is built on \emph{ṭhokar}, \textquotedblleft{}a kick, a blow\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ṭhokar} under \emph{*ṭhōkk}, \textquotedblleft{}knock\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5513). To push a thing away with the foot.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhukrānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhukrānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jalse ne us kī tajvīz ṭhukrā dī.} — The meeting flatly turned down his proposal.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a district, then the Urdu for a majority, then say \emph{ṭhukrānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
